  422  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
  423  
  424  Commands added using the Flask app's :attr:`~Flask.cli` or
  425  :class:`~flask.cli.FlaskGroup` :meth:`~cli.AppGroup.command` decorator
  426  will be executed with an application context pushed, so your custom
  427  commands and parameters have access to the app and its configuration. The
  428  :func:`~cli.with_appcontext` decorator can be used to get the same
  429  behavior, but is not needed in most cases.
  430  
  431  .. code-block:: python
  432  
  433      import click
  434      from flask.cli import with_appcontext
  435  
  436      @click.command()
  437      @with_appcontext
  438      def do_work():
  439          ...
  440  
  441      app.cli.add_command(do_work)
  442  
  443  
  444  Plugins
  445  -------
  446  
  447  Flask will automatically load commands specified in the ``flask.commands``
  448  `entry point`_. This is useful for extensions that want to add commands when
  449  they are installed. Entry points are specified in :file:`pyproject.toml`:
  450  
  451  .. code-block:: toml
  452  
  453      [project.entry-points."flask.commands"]
  454      my-command = "my_extension.commands:cli"
  455  
  456  .. _entry point: https://packaging.python.org/tutorials/packaging-projects/#entry-points
  457  
  458  Inside :file:`my_extension/commands.py` you can then export a Click
  459  object::
  460  
  461      import click
  462  
  463      @click.command()
  464      def cli():
  465          ...
  466  
  467  Once that package is installed in the same virtualenv as your Flask project,
  468  you can run ``flask my-command`` to invoke the command.
  469  
  470  
  471  .. _custom-scripts:
  472  
  473  Custom Scripts
  474  --------------
  475  
  476  When you are using the app factory pattern, it may be more convenient to define
  477  your own Click script. Instead of using ``--app`` and letting Flask load
  478  your application, you can create your own Click object and export it as a
  479  `console script`_ entry point.
  480  
  481  Create an instance of :class:`~cli.FlaskGroup` and pass it the factory::
  482  
  483      import click
  484      from flask import Flask
  485      from flask.cli import FlaskGroup
  486  
  487      def create_app():
  488          app = Flask('wiki')
  489          # other setup
  490          return app
  491  
  492      @click.group(cls=FlaskGroup, create_app=create_app)
  493      def cli():
  494          """Management script for the Wiki application."""
  495  
  496  Define the entry point in :file:`pyproject.toml`:
  497  
  498  .. code-block:: toml
  499  
  500      [project.scripts]
  501      wiki = "wiki:cli"
  502  
  503  Install the application in the virtualenv in editable mode and the custom
  504  script is available. Note that you don't need to set ``--app``. ::
  505  
  506      $ pip install -e .
  507      $ wiki run
  508  
  509  .. admonition:: Errors in Custom Scripts
  510  
  511      When using a custom script, if you introduce an error in your
  512      module-level code, the reloader will fail because it can no longer
  513      load the entry point.
  514  
  515      The ``flask`` command, being separate from your code, does not have
  516      this issue and is recommended in most cases.
  517  
  518  .. _console script: https://packaging.python.org/tutorials/packagi
